task.situation: You have received an email from Ravi, an English friend you met at a summer camp last year. Ravi promised his best friend, Chloe, that he would come to her birthday party last Saturday. But he completely forgot and went to a football match with his uncle instead. Now Chloe is angry and hasn’t answered any of his messages. Ravi asks you what he should do.
task.instruction: Write a reply to Ravi. In your email you should:
points: show that you understand how Ravi feels
advise him how to apologise to Chloe
suggest what he could do to make it up to her
task.de: Informelle Antwort-E-Mail an einen englischen Freund, der den Geburtstag seiner besten Freundin vergessen und damit ein Versprechen gebrochen hat. Drei Inhaltspunkte: Verständnis zeigen; raten, wie er sich entschuldigen soll; vorschlagen, wie er es wiedergutmachen kann. Freundlicher, persönlicher Ton, Kurzformen erlaubt.

focus.label: should / could / if I were you
focus.labelDe: Ratschläge: should, could, if I were you
focus.note: Marked: phrases for giving advice and making suggestions: should / shouldn’t, could and If I were you, I’d … (from ‘If’ to ‘I’d’). Other modal verbs (can, will, would, might) are not marked.

gaps.q: Who is writing to Ravi? First name only.
gaps.qDe: Ruft einen Vornamen für die Person, die Ravi antwortet. Keine Namen von Mitschüler:innen oder Lehrer:innen.

steps.q: What do we write in the subject line?
steps.de: Die Betreffzeile sagt in wenigen Wörtern, worum es in der Antwort geht.
steps.own: Short and friendly: what is your reply about?
steps.ownDe: Kurz und freundlich: Worum geht es in eurer Antwort?

options.label: A reply
options.text: Re: Chloe’s birthday party
options.why: ‘Re:’ shows that this is a reply, so Ravi finds it at once.

options.label: Calm him down
options.text: Don’t panic, Ravi!
options.why: Friendly and short. It already tells Ravi that things are not so bad.

options.label: Name the topic
options.text: My advice about Chloe
options.why: Clear: Ravi knows what the email is about before he opens it.

steps.de: Hier wählen wir die Anrede für einen Freund. Prüft jede Option: Aufgabe, Aufbau, Wortschatz, Grammatik.
steps.own: Copy the greeting. Then leave one line free.
steps.ownDe: Anrede abschreiben, danach eine Zeile frei lassen.

options.label: Hi
options.text: {{Hi Ravi,}}
options.why: Friendly and informal, just right for a friend.

options.label: Dear
options.text: {{Dear Ravi,}}
options.why: ‘Dear’ with a first name is warm and works in a personal email too.

steps.q: Introduction: how do we react to Ravi’s email?
steps.de: Die Einleitung reagiert auf Ravis E-Mail und kündigt Hilfe an. Prüft jede Option: Aufgabe, Aufbau, Wortschatz, Grammatik.
steps.own: Copy the frame. Then finish the paragraph: react to Ravi’s news and say that you want to help.
steps.ownDe: Gerüst abschreiben, dann den Absatz fertigschreiben: auf Ravis Nachricht reagieren und Hilfe anbieten.

options.label: Thank him and react
options.text: {{Thanks for your email.}} I was sorry to hear about you and Chloe, but I’m glad you wrote to me. {{I think I’ve got a few ideas}} that might help.
options.why: It thanks Ravi, reacts to his news and tells him what the email will bring.

options.label: Thank him for his news
options.text: Thanks for your email! Guess what happened to me last weekend: my volleyball team won the regional cup, and I scored the last point! Anyway, about Chloe: I’m sure it’s not a big deal.
options.reject: Ravi is upset, but this opening is mostly about our own weekend, and ‘it’s not a big deal’ shows that we don’t take his problem seriously.
options.rejectDe: Ravi geht es schlecht, aber die Einleitung handelt fast nur vom eigenen Wochenende, und „it’s not a big deal“ nimmt sein Problem nicht ernst.

options.label: React with feeling
options.text: {{Thanks for writing to me. What a horrible week}} you’ve had! I’ve read your email twice and thought about you and Chloe a lot. {{Here are a few ideas}} that might help you.
options.why: An exclamation shows that we care, and the last sentence leads to our advice.

steps.q: Body paragraph 1: how do we show that we understand Ravi?
steps.de: Erster Inhaltspunkt: Verständnis für Ravi zeigen. Prüft jede Option: Aufgabe, Aufbau, Wortschatz, Grammatik.
steps.own: Copy the frame. Then add two sentences of your own that show you understand Ravi.
steps.ownDe: Gerüst abschreiben, dann zwei eigene Sätze ergänzen, die Verständnis für Ravi zeigen.

options.label: Show sympathy
options.text: {{First of all, I can imagine how}} terrible you feel. Forgetting a party can happen to anyone, and you didn’t do it on purpose. {{You [[shouldn’t]] be too hard on yourself.}} It was a mistake, and you can still fix it.
options.why: It shows sympathy and gives Ravi hope before the advice starts.
options.textLong: {{First of all, I can imagine how}} terrible you feel. Forgetting a party can happen to anyone, and you didn’t do it on purpose. I’m sure you were excited about the match with your uncle, and the date simply slipped your mind. {{You [[shouldn’t]] be too hard on yourself.}} One mistake doesn’t make you a bad friend, and you can still fix it.

options.label: See both sides
options.text: {{I understand why you feel so bad, but}} I can see Chloe’s side, too. She was probably looking forward to seeing you, and now she must be really disappointed. {{Still, you [[shouldn’t]] give up on}} your friendship. It’s worth saving.
options.why: Understanding for Ravi and for Chloe prepares honest advice.
options.textLong: {{I understand why you feel so bad, but}} I can see Chloe’s side, too. She was probably looking forward to seeing you, and now she must be really disappointed. Maybe she even waited for you before she cut the cake. {{Still, you [[shouldn’t]] give up on}} your friendship. You and Chloe have been best friends for a long time, and that’s worth saving.

options.label: A similar story
options.text: {{Believe me, I know exactly how you feel.}} Last year I forgot my cousin’s birthday, and she didn’t speak to me for a week. I felt awful, but we’re close again now. {{That’s why you [[shouldn’t]] lose hope:}} this can be fixed.
options.why: A short story of our own shows Ravi that he is not alone and that things can get better.
options.textLong: {{Believe me, I know exactly how you feel.}} Last year I forgot my cousin’s birthday, and she didn’t speak to me for a week. I felt awful and kept checking my phone for a message from her. After a long talk we were close again, and today we can laugh about it. {{That’s why you [[shouldn’t]] lose hope:}} this can be fixed.

steps.ownLong: Copy the frame. Then add three sentences of your own that show you understand Ravi.
steps.ownLongDe: Gerüst abschreiben, dann drei eigene Sätze ergänzen, die Verständnis für Ravi zeigen.

steps.q: Body paragraph 2: how should Ravi apologise?
steps.de: Zweiter Inhaltspunkt: Ratschläge, wie Ravi sich bei Chloe entschuldigen soll. Prüft jede Option: Aufgabe, Aufbau, Wortschatz, Grammatik.
steps.own: Copy the frame. Then give Ravi two pieces of advice in your own words.
steps.ownDe: Gerüst abschreiben, dann Ravi zwei eigene Ratschläge geben.

options.label: Talk face to face
options.text: {{So how [[should]] you say sorry? [[If I were you, I’d]] talk to Chloe face to face}} instead of sending another message. Tell her honestly what happened, and don’t make excuses. {{You [[shouldn’t]] blame}} the football match or your uncle because that will only make her angrier.
options.why: A question leads to the advice, ‘If I were you, I’d …’ gives it, and ‘shouldn’t’ warns Ravi what not to do.
options.textLong: {{So how [[should]] you say sorry? [[If I were you, I’d]] talk to Chloe face to face}} instead of sending another message. Tell her honestly what happened, and don’t make excuses. {{You [[shouldn’t]] blame}} the football match or your uncle because that will only make her angrier. Then be patient: she may need a few days to forgive you.

options.label: Write a letter
options.text: {{To put things right, the first thing you [[should]] do is apologise properly.}} Chloe isn’t answering your messages, so you [[could]] write her a real letter by hand. {{In the letter, explain}} what happened and tell her how much your friendship means to you.
options.why: ‘Should’ for the most important advice, ‘could’ for a softer suggestion with a clear plan.
options.textLong: {{To put things right, the first thing you [[should]] do is apologise properly.}} Chloe isn’t answering your messages, so you [[could]] write her a real letter by hand. {{In the letter, explain}} what happened and tell her how much your friendship means to you. Put it through her letterbox. That way, she can read it alone and in peace.

options.label: Go and see her
options.text: If I would be you, I would go to her house and explain her what happened. Don’t send another message because she is still angry. You should also make her a small present, for example a card with a nice photo of you two from the summer.
options.reject: Three typical mistakes: ‘If I would be you’ (→ If I were you), ‘explain her’ (→ explain to her) and ‘make her a present’ (→ give her a present).
options.rejectDe: Drei typische Fehler: If I would be you → If I were you, explain her → explain to her, make a present (Geschenk machen) → give a present.
options.textLong: If I would be you, I would go to her house and explain her what happened. Don’t send another message because she is still angry. You should also make her a small present, for example a card with a nice photo of you two from the summer. Hand it to her at the door and give her time to think.

steps.ownLong: Copy the frame. Then give Ravi two pieces of advice in your own words and add a reason for one of them.
steps.ownLongDe: Gerüst abschreiben, dann Ravi zwei eigene Ratschläge geben und einen davon begründen.

steps.q: Body paragraph 3: what could Ravi do to make it up to Chloe?
steps.de: Dritter Inhaltspunkt: Vorschläge, wie Ravi seinen Fehler wiedergutmachen kann. Prüft jede Option: Aufgabe, Aufbau, Wortschatz, Grammatik.
steps.own: Copy the frame. Then suggest one idea of your own and say why it would help.
steps.ownDe: Gerüst abschreiben, dann eine eigene Idee vorschlagen und sagen, warum sie helfen würde.

options.label: A picnic and a cake
options.text: After the apology, you could have a picnic with her. Choose her favourite park. Bake a cake. Write ‘Sorry!’ on it in big letters. Take some music, too. She will see that you care. She will smile. Then your friendship will be fine again.
options.reject: The idea is good, but there are only very short, simple sentences, one after the other. Join your ideas: a picnic in her favourite park, with a cake that says ‘Sorry!’ …
options.rejectDe: Gute Idee, aber nur sehr kurze, einfache Sätze hintereinander: Gedanken verbinden, z. B. mit Relativsätzen (that, which) und Linking words.
options.textLong: After the apology, you could have a picnic with her. Choose her favourite park. Bring a blanket. Pack some sandwiches and drinks. Bake a chocolate cake. Write ‘Sorry!’ on it in big letters. Take some music, too. She will see that you care. She will smile. Then your friendship will be fine again.

options.label: A late birthday surprise
options.text: {{After your apology, you [[could]] organise}} a small late birthday surprise for her. What about a picnic in her favourite park, or a cake with ‘Sorry!’ on it? {{But you [[shouldn’t]] make it too big,}} or it might look like you are trying to buy her forgiveness.
options.why: ‘Could’ and ‘What about …?’ make suggestions, and ‘shouldn’t’ adds a sensible warning.
options.textLong: {{After your apology, you [[could]] organise}} a small late birthday surprise for her. What about a picnic in her favourite park, or a cake with ‘Sorry!’ on it? You [[could]] even ask one of her friends what she would like best. {{But you [[shouldn’t]] make it too big,}} or it might look like you are trying to buy her forgiveness.

options.label: Spend time together
options.text: {{When you’ve said sorry, you [[could]] invite her}} to something she loves, like a concert, the ice rink or a day at the lake. {{The most important thing is}} that you spend time together. Maybe you [[should]] let her choose the plan this time.
options.why: A concrete suggestion with examples, then the reason behind it.
options.textLong: {{When you’ve said sorry, you [[could]] invite her}} to something she loves, like a concert, the ice rink or a day at the lake. {{The most important thing is}} that you spend time together, just the two of you and without phones. Maybe you [[should]] let her choose the plan this time, and you [[could]] promise to be there on time!

steps.ownLong: Copy the frame. Then suggest two ideas of your own and say why they would help.
steps.ownLongDe: Gerüst abschreiben, dann zwei eigene Ideen vorschlagen und sagen, warum sie helfen würden.

steps.q: Conclusion: how do we end the email?
steps.de: Der Schluss fasst die Ratschläge kurz zusammen, macht Mut und bittet um eine Antwort. Prüft jede Option: Aufgabe, Aufbau, Wortschatz, Grammatik.
steps.own: Copy the frame. Then add one encouraging sentence of your own for Ravi.
steps.ownDe: Gerüst abschreiben, dann einen eigenen Satz ergänzen, der Ravi Mut macht.

options.label: Wish him luck
options.text: {{Good luck, Ravi!}} I know you feel bad now, but if you say sorry honestly and show Chloe that she matters to you, she’ll forgive you. {{Write back soon and tell me how it went.}}
options.why: It sums up the advice in one sentence, encourages Ravi and asks for a reply.

options.label: A little news from us
options.text: {{Well, I hope my ideas help.}} An honest apology and a little time together can fix a lot. Things are fine here, although I’ve got two tests next week. {{Let me know}} what happens, and keep your chin up!
options.why: It picks up the advice, adds a little news of our own and keeps Ravi’s problem the main topic.

options.label: Wish him luck and ask for news
options.text: Good luck, Ravi! I’m sure Chloe will forgive you. Nevertheless, you’ve been friends for years, and one forgotten party can’t destroy that. Otherwise, write back soon and tell me how it went.
options.reject: The linking words don’t fit: ‘Nevertheless’ introduces a contrast, but here a reason follows (→ After all). ‘Otherwise’ means ‘if not’, not ‘apart from that’ (→ Anyway).
options.rejectDe: Die Linking words passen nicht: Nevertheless kündigt einen Gegensatz an, hier folgt aber ein Grund (→ After all). Otherwise heißt „falls nicht“, nicht „sonst noch“ (→ Anyway).

steps.de: Am Ende stehen die Grußformel und darunter der Vorname, den ihr gleich selbst bestimmt. Prüft jede Option: Aufgabe, Aufbau, Wortschatz, Grammatik.
steps.own: Copy the closing formula and, on the next line, the first name we chose.
steps.ownDe: Grußformel abschreiben, darunter den gewählten Vornamen.

options.label: Take care
options.text:
{{Take care,}}
{NAME}
options.why: Friendly and caring, a good ending when a friend has a problem.

options.label: Best wishes
options.text:
{{Best wishes,}}
{NAME}
options.why: Polite and friendly, good for many personal emails.

checks.en: A subject line that fits the reply
Informal greeting and sign-off for a friend
Each content point has its own body paragraph, in the order of the task
All three content points: understanding, how to apologise, how to make it up
A range of advice phrases: should, shouldn’t, could, If I were you, I’d …
Each piece of advice comes with a reason or an example
Friendly, personal tone: contractions are fine, mistakes are not
The last paragraph encourages Ravi and asks him to write back

teacher.aim: Die Klasse baut gemeinsam eine informelle Antwort-E-Mail (A2+/B1) an einen Freund, der den Geburtstag seiner besten Freundin vergessen hat, und übt dabei Ratschläge und Vorschläge mit should / shouldn’t, could und If I were you, I’d … sowie die Konventionen der informellen E-Mail.
teacher.prep: A/B/C/D-Karten austeilen (eine Garnitur pro Person), Hefte bereitlegen. Beamer im Vollbild. Im Gerüst-Modus den eingebauten Timer nutzen: 5 min pro Absatz, bei Bedarf +1. Die Aufgabe am Beamer enthält alles Nötige.
teacher.heft: Neue Seite: Datum rechts oben, darunter „Email“ als Überschrift (wie am Beamer). Darunter der E-Mail-Kopf mit vier Zeilen (To, From, Date, Subject) wie am Beamer; der Betreff kommt nach der ersten Entscheidung in die Subject-Zeile, der Name erst unter die Grußformel. Anrede in einer eigenen Zeile, dann eine Zeile frei. Fünf Absätze, jeder nach einer Leerzeile, am Rand die Randwörter Intro, Body 1, Body 2, Body 3, Conclusion. Vor der Grußformel eine Zeile frei, dann Grußformel und Name in zwei eigenen Zeilen. Ratschlag-Wendungen grün unterstreichen.
teacher.flow: Volltext kurz (50 min): 5 min Aufgabe lesen, 8 Entscheidungen (Betreff, Anrede und Grußformel je ca. 1 min, die fünf Absätze je ca. 2 min), Abschreiben ca. 20 min, 5 min Checkliste. Volltext lang (ca. 60 min): dieselben 8 Entscheidungen; die drei Hauptabsätze sind je rund 15 Wörter länger, das Abschreiben dauert daher ca. 30 min. In einer Doppelstunde die restliche Zeit für die Besprechung der Fallen nutzen und die Hausübung zu zweit beginnen. Gerüst kurz (realistisch ca. 60 min): 5 min Aufgabe; Betreff, Anrede und Grußformel je ca. 1 min; pro Absatz 1 min Entscheidung, 5–6 min eigenes Schreiben, 1 min Vergleich mit dem Modell; am Ende 5 min Checkliste. In einer 50-Minuten-Stunde bei der Conclusion nur abstimmen und das Gerüst abschreiben lassen, den eigenen Satz als Hausübung. Gerüst lang (ca. 70 min): dieselben 8 Entscheidungen im gleichen Rhythmus, bei den drei Hauptabsätzen je ca. 3 min mehr eigenes Schreiben (ein Satz bzw. ein Rat mehr). In einer Doppelstunde danach eine Vergleichsrunde zu zweit.
teacher.traps: Introduction B (TA): erzählt fast nur vom eigenen Wochenende und nimmt Ravis Problem nicht ernst. Body 2 C (LSA): If I would be you (→ If I were you), explain her (→ explain to her), make her a present (→ give her a present). Body 3 A (LSR): nur sehr kurze, einfache Sätze hintereinander, nichts ist verbunden (besser: a picnic in her favourite park, with a cake that says ‘Sorry!’). Conclusion C (CC): Nevertheless vor einem Grund, Otherwise im Sinn von „sonst noch“. Kürzel: TA = Erfüllung der Aufgabenstellung, CC = Kohärenz und Kohäsion, LSR = Spektrum sprachlicher Mittel, LSA = Sprachrichtigkeit.
teacher.notes: Aufbau: Jede E-Mail hat fünf Absätze (Einleitung, drei Hauptabsätze mit je einem Inhaltspunkt, Schluss); die lange Fassung hat dieselben Entscheidungen, nur die drei Hauptabsätze sind länger; sie fügt keinen Absatz hinzu. Thema Freundschaft: Es geht um einen alltäglichen Fehler (vergessene Party, gebrochenes Versprechen), nicht um Mobbing. Im Gerüst-Modus nicht nach eigenen Streitigkeiten fragen; die Ratschläge beziehen sich auf Ravi und Chloe. Ravi, Chloe und die Adressen sind erfunden; für die Namenslücke nur erfundene Vornamen verwenden, keine Namen von Mitschüler:innen oder Lehrer:innen. Fokus: Nach Body 2 an der Tafel sammeln: If I were you, I’d … (nie „If I would be“), You should / shouldn’t …, You could …, What about …?, Why don’t you …? Differenzierung: Schnelle ergänzen im Gerüst-Modus einen Satz mit „Why don’t you …?“. Hausübung: Ravis Antwort (ca. 80 Wörter): Was hat er gemacht, und wie hat Chloe reagiert?
